title: Multiomics Data Integration for Chromatin Remodeling Analysis
author: Yun, Vohra, et al.

steps.title: Prepare computational environment
steps.instruction: Install all required bioinformatics tools (e.g., FastQC, Bowtie2/BWA, STAR, MACS2, DESeq2, CHiCAGO) on hardware that meets the minimum specifications described in the protocol and place the exemplar NGS data sets in an accessible directory.

steps.title: Quality‑control raw reads
steps.instruction: Run a quality‑control program (e.g., FastQC) on each raw FASTQ file to assess read quality, adapter contamination, and duplication rates.

steps.title: Map reads to reference genome
steps.instruction: Align ATAC‑seq, ChIP‑seq, pCHiC, and RNA‑seq reads to the mouse reference genome using appropriate aligners (e.g., Bowtie2 for ATAC/ChIP, STAR for RNA‑seq) with default parameters.

steps.title: Filter and normalize alignments
steps.instruction: Remove low‑quality alignments, PCR duplicates, and mitochondrial reads; then normalize read counts (e.g., CPM or RPKM) for each data type as required for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Call peaks and interactions
steps.instruction: For ATAC‑seq, call peaks with MACS2 using a p‑value cutoff of 1e‑20. For pCHiC data, identify significant chromatin interactions with CHiCAGO using a score threshold of ≥5.

steps.title: Integrate chromatin state data
steps.instruction: Combine ATAC‑seq peaks, histone‑modification data, and pCHiC interaction calls across the four cellular states to define dynamic chromatin states and cluster cis‑regulatory elements (CREs) that show similar modification dynamics.

steps.title: Annotate CRE clusters to genes
steps.instruction: Assign each CRE cluster to putative target genes based on linear proximity (nearest gene) or spatial proximity using the significant chromatin loops identified in the pCHiC analysis.

steps.title: Differential expression analysis
steps.instruction: Use DESeq2 to compare RNA‑seq count data between conditions, calculate two‑tailed P values, adjust them with the Benjamini‑Hochberg method, and consider genes with adjusted P ≤0.05 as statistically significant.

steps.title: Functional network analysis
steps.instruction: Perform pathway enrichment and construct functional gene‑interaction networks for the differentially expressed genes identified in the previous step.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for performing the integrative analysis of chromatin accessibility, chromatin states, DNA looping and transcriptome across four cellular states in a murine allelic series that models the two most common mutations in acute myeloid leukemia (AML): Flt3-ITD and Npm1c, both of which are present in 15%–20% of all AML cases. Either of the two mutations alone caused mild and pre-malignant phenotype, whereas in combination they demonstrated strong synergistic effect to induce aggressive AML. The hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), a bulk cell population represented by the lineage negative (Lin-) fraction of bone marrow cells harvested from wildtype (WT), single mutant (Flt3-ITD or Npm1c), and double mutant (DM, both Flt3-ITD and Npm1c) mice, were used to generate all the multiomics data as an exemplar in this protocol. This section includes minimum requirements for computer hardware, pre-installation of software (including tools and algorithms) for data processing, as well as a collection of exemplar next generation sequencing (NGS) data to be analyzed. Herein we describe step-by-step analytical procedures starting from raw data processing all the way through to integrated data analysis. The raw data undergo serial processing steps covering: quality control, read mapping, data filtering, normalization, and statistical calling. Subsequently, the processed data are first subjected to integrated analysis on dynamic chromatin states, to reveal differential clusters of cis-regulatory elements (CREs) that demonstrate similar dynamic chromatin modifications. Afterwards, the specific clusters of CREs with characteristic gain or loss of enhancer signatures are annotated to target genes, using either linear or spatial proximity information.
